findings.change_summary: Status re-confirmed as shelved (unchanged); strengthened the citation from one weak-inference source to two independent, non-mirror sources. Chain: matuwid.org's mirror of the Dec 8 2023 Manila Standard/DOE report (verified: 'Tabangao', 'September 2025') is the last known forward-looking milestone -- Shell Energy Philippines' Tabangao FSRU was DOE-targeted to begin commercial operations by September 2025 at 3 MTPA. That target date has now passed (current date July 2026) with zero commissioning/inauguration news anywhere (checked LNG Prime, offshore-technology.com, BusinessWorld, Manila Bulletin, Manila Standard, Philstar, PNA, industry roundups). The May 13 2025 Manila Bulletin piece (verified: 'Tabangao') is Shell Pilipinas' own capital-spending announcement for the Tabangao site and covers ONLY the oil-products import facility (fuel storage/gantry) and mobility/gas-station spend -- it makes zero mention of the LNG/FSRU project despite being exactly the kind of announcement that would flag it if alive. A further Sept 22 2025 Manila Bulletin piece on Shell Energy Philippines' (SEPH -- the actual LNG project developer) capex priorities (solar, battery, onshore wind) also contains no LNG/gas mention (checked but not cited as a ref since it never names Tabangao directly). Current published rosters of Philippine Batangas-area import terminals (as of 2025-2026) list only FGEN Batangas FSRU and the AG&P/Philippines LNG Terminal as operating -- Shell's own Tabangao FSRU is absent from all of them, consistent with the inferred-shelved call. No source found announcing formal cancellation, so 'inferred 2 y' substatus (not 'confirmed') remains correct; keep ShelvedYear 2025 (the point at which the missed Sept-2025 DOE target plus ~2 years of silence since the last real project update crystallized the inference).

findings.new_value: Lifecycle note: ConstructionYear=2024 reflects a DOE-reported PLANNED/target construction start (per Dec 2023 Manila Standard/DOE data citing a Sept-2025 commercial-ops target), not an actual confirmed construction event -- consistent with the GEM status_timeline carrying both the 2024 construction and 2025 operating entries as substatus 'planned', never 'actual'. No source found confirms ground was ever broken, an FSRU was chartered/named, or the jetty conversion (Jetty 4) proceeded. The Sept-2025 target has passed with no commissioning news and no mention of the project in Shell's own 2025-2026 Tabangao/SEPH capex announcements, so 'shelved (inferred 2 y)' correctly describes current status -- there is no construction/shelved contradiction, just an unactualized forecast year sitting alongside the correct current status.

summary: Resolved: Tabangao FSRU remains correctly SHELVED (inferred 2 y, anchor year 2025) -- no status change staged. The apparent construction/shelved contradiction is not a real contradiction: ConstructionYear=2024 and the 2025 'operating' timeline entry are both DOE-reported PLANNED targets (per a Dec 2023 Manila Standard/DOE report citing a Sept-2025 commercial-ops target for Shell Energy Philippines' 3 MTPA FSRU), never marked 'actual' in the timeline, and no source shows the project ever actually broke ground or chartered an FSRU. That Sept-2025 target has now passed with total silence: Shell's own May 2025 and Sept 2025 Tabangao/SEPH capex announcements make zero mention of the LNG project, and current Philippine Batangas-terminal rosters list only FGEN Batangas FSRU and the AG&P/Philippines LNG Terminal as operating, not Shell. Strengthened the Status [ref] citation from one weak single source to two independent verified sources; added a ResearcherNotesProject note explaining the planned-vs-actual distinction for future researchers. No FSRU vessel was ever named (FloatingVesselName stays blank); no new entities needed.
